simple.meaning: bird of prey , usually thought to be the pelican (from casting itself into the sea)
simple.inThisVerse: The selected word is tied to שָׁלָךְ (H7994) in the Hebrew source text. Part of speech: n-m.
simple.whyItMatters: This word appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, so BibleIQ can compare how Scripture uses it across multiple passages.
simple.summary: שָׁלָךְ (shâlâk) means bird of prey , usually thought to be the pelican (from casting itself into the sea) First listed occurrence: Deut 14 17.

definitions.short: bird of prey , usually thought to be the pelican (from casting itself into the sea)
definitions.full: H7994. shalak שָׁלָךְ noun [masculine] bird of prey , probably cormorant (as hurling itself from above; — compare Thes 1419 Di Lv Tristr NHB 252 McLean-Shipley Ency.Bib.CORMORANT ); — Deut 14:17 ; Lev 11:17 ; (P).
